messages:
raji: heads-up — saw a 20-35% token-latency regression on the 8-card hybrid TP+PP job after we enabled activation checkpointing on the 16B model. reproducer attached in the perf run.

maya: ugh. is this steady-state or during KV-cache warmup?

raji: steady-state. KV cache warmup adds a bit but the bulk is in increased all-reduce stalls during backward. nvprof-like timeline shows long idle gaps on ranks 2/5. i'll paste the snippet:
```
Backward step 102: compute 45ms | all-reduce 78ms | overlap 5ms | idle 32ms
Forward step 103: compute 12ms | kv-io 3ms
```

kyle: interesting — that all-reduce jump smells like recompute-caused fragmentation of the pipe. checkpointing changed the schedule so gradient chunks aren't aligned across TP shards.

ananya: can you share which kernels are firing? kernel selection could amplify this if we fall back to slower kernels under different buffer shapes.

raji: yes. before checkpointing we used cutlass-fused attention kernels for seq=1024. After checkpointing, the activation rematerialization increases activation sizes during backward, and we see a fallback to cuBLAS GEMM for the last matmul on some ranks. sample:
```
rank 0: cutlass_attn_fused :: 28ms
rank 2: cuBLAS_gemm        :: 64ms
```

maya: that mismatch + larger all-reduce = double whammy. cpus show higher memcpy from device->host on those ranks too. are we still using NCCL tree vs ring?

kyle: cluster uses NCCL ring by default but we have a topology-aware tree option enabled for some pools. iirc the tree mode had better overlap historically, but only if compute bursts align. If checkpointing staggers compute, tree degenerates.

ananya: what about batching heuristics? are we microbatching differently now because of memory pressure?

raji: yes — to fit memory with checkpointing we increased microbatch to 4 -> 6 and reduced per-step kernel fusion. That increases the frequency of all-reduce calls (more smaller all-reduces) which hurts throughput.

maya: quick thought: two orthogonal mitigations: 1) re-align recompute boundaries to keep gradient chunk sizes consistent across TP shards (reduce fragmentation). 2) adjust accumulation so we do fewer larger all-reduces (increase accumulate steps) and rely on asynchronous all-reduce + CUDA streams.

kyle: +1. Also test forcing the cutlass kernel selection via env override to confirm kernel fallback is contributing. try setting REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=cutlass_attn for one run.

raji: will run both: (A) align checkpoints at transformer block boundaries (stagger off), (B) lower microbatch count and increase grad accumulation to keep effective batch but fewer all-reduces, (C) force kernel selection.

ananya: please also dump KV-cache RPC timing. if checkpointing delays forward write-backs, subsequent requests might wait on stale KV flushes which shows up as per-token tail latency. we saw that in a different run.

raji: noted. KV dump attached in run-439. early look: KV IO stays small (~2-4ms) but serialization spikes when some ranks are stuck in all-reduce — so it's secondary cascading effect.

maya: timeline hypothesis: checkpointing -> rematerialize bursts -> kernel fallback on subset of ranks -> misaligned compute windows -> more/smaller all-reduces -> increased NCCL latency -> idle on other ranks -> KV flushes pile up.

kyle: sounds right. if we can't avoid extra compute from remat, we can try: - kernel pinning, - schedule-based padding to align windows, - ring->tree toggling, - congestion-aware all-reduce coalescing.

raji: running 3 experiments now across 8-card pool: exp1 align checkpoints, exp2 grad-accumulate tuning, exp3 kernel pin override. will report perf numbers in ~45m. posting profiler flame GIF to the thread when done.

ci-bot: perf-job 439 started on pool-8gpu (config: align-checkpoints=true, acc_steps=3, kernel_override=cutlass). logs: https://ci.internal/runs/439

ananya: thanks — on the docs side i'll sketch a short checklist for devs: when enabling activation checkpointing -> verify kernel selection, validate TP shard alignment, confirm all-reduce size distribution, and measure KV tail latencies.

maya: good plan. if exp1+2 recover >10% we can include staging rollout with gating metric = tokens/sec regression <5%.

raji: quick interim numbers: exp1 (align) -> 12% improvement; exp2 (accumulate) -> 18% improvement; exp3 (force kernel) -> 5% improvement but caused OOM on one config (we're tuning workspace). attaching raw numbers.

kyle: nice. does that mean a combined strategy should bring us back to baseline or better?

raji: combining align+accumulate gives ~28% recovered vs baseline-with-checkpointing. still ~7% behind no-checkpoint baseline, likely due to extra recompute compute cost.

ananya: decision: for the rollout, enable activation checkpointing by default only with our alignment patch + grad-accumulation defaults. include kernel-selection guardrails in runtime (auto-fallback if OOM). I'll open a PR for the config defaults.

maya: and add a perf test that runs with checkpointing toggled to catch regressions in CI (token/sec and NCCL tail p95).

raji: opened PR #2781 for alignment patch and #2782 for CI perf. will follow-up with annotated timeline and kernel traces. :thumbsup:

kyle: thanks everyone. ping me if the forced kernel runs blow up — we can automate kernel probing at startup instead of forcing.
